decisions.reason: The authors explicitly define a secondary purpose as replicating Lanovaz and Hranchuk (2021) on new clinical data, distinct from the primary Wolfe et al. (2018) comparison. The reference identifies DOI 10.1002/jaba.863; the sole shipped pair is Wolfe (10.1002/jaba.453). Parent reviewed the cited results/purpose and reference identity against all supplied shipped originals. This decision confirms the missing paper-level pair only; its overall outcome has not been adjudicated.

decisions.quote:
The purpose of our study was to replicate and extend Wolfe et al. (2018) by examining agreement between visual inspection and the conservative dual-criteria method. We extended Wolfe et al. by using a larger number of graphs to examine within-subject error, blinded normalized graphs, and modified reversal/withdrawal designs.
A secondary purpose was to replicate and extend Lanovaz and Hranchuk (2021) by examining correspondence between visual inspection, the conservative dual-criteria method, and the machine-learning algorithms on a novel dataset. We extended both studies by using clinical data and adding a 10-point scale with definitional criteria to visual-inspection ratings.
decisions.reason: The study explicitly re-tests the finding of Wolfe et al. (2018) regarding agreement between expert visual inspection and the conservative dual-criteria method using a new sample of 198 clinical single-case AB phase-comparison graphs and new ratings from five doctoral-level behavior analysts. Collecting and analyzing new data/samples to re-test a published finding is a replication under the codebook, confirming both the shipped and blind coding.
